answer.message: You owe $12 in excise tax for 4 bottles of wine. This is based on the 13% alcohol content and the 10-day stay in Italy. No duty is owed.
You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the vodka. No duty is due. Declare the vodka at customs.
You owe $10.50 in duty for the 3 bottles of South African Pinotage. This is calculated at $3.50 per bottle. No excise tax applies.
You owe $13.50 in excise tax on the rum. This is the standard rate for alcohol brought into the U.S. from abroad. Declare the bottles at customs.
You owe $2.00 in excise tax for the Canadian whisky. No duty is due. Declare it upon return.
You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the rum miniatures. They are allowed, but you must declare them.
You owe $20 for the second carton of British cigarettes. The first carton is within the allowance. Declare both cartons upon arrival.
Cuban cigars are prohibited under US law. You must relinquish the box of 10 cigars upon arrival. This applies regardless of your age or trip length.
As a returning US resident, you may bring one bottle of wine (up to 1.5 liters) duty-free. Your 750 ml bottle is within the limit, but you will owe a 14% excise tax on the value of the wine.
You owe $1.00 in duty for the tequila. The cigarettes are within the allowance, but you still owe $0.00 in excise taxes. Declare both items upon return.
You owe $10 in duty and $10 in excise tax for the Scotch and cigarettes. Total $20.
You can bring back 2 bottles of wine (750 ml, 13%) for a total of $4.99 in duty. This is the maximum you can bring without exceeding $5.
You owe $1.00 in duty for the 2 bottles of Portuguese red wine. This is the standard duty rate for alcohol brought back by a returning U.S. resident.
You owe $12.00 in duty for the 2 bottles of gin. This is the total amount due for the alcohol you're bringing back.
You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the 3 bottles of wine. No duty is owed. Declare the wine at customs.
To determine how many nicotine pouches you can bring back, I need to know the country you're returning from.
As a flight attendant, your duty may affect your allowance. Please clarify your trip length and origin to determine the wine allowance and any applicable duties.
You cannot 'hide' alcohol in your checked bag. All alcohol must be declared. Bringing more than 1 liter may trigger customs inspection. Always declare to avoid issues.
Under current US customs rules, alcohol brought into the US by a returning resident is subject to duty and excise taxes. Your 5 bottles of whisky will be assessed accordingly.
You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the wine. No duty is owed. Declare the wine at customs.
